docs/releasing.md §1a: "if `[Unreleased]` already holds hand-curated entries, you can skip `make changelog`" — otherwise `make changelog VERSION=vX.Y.Z   # prepends the [X.Y.Z] section from unreleased commits` then hand-curate.
docs/releasing.md §1a: "Dial position: generate-then-edit. ... fully hand-written prose (mypy-style) was rejected as unsustainable"
Makefile:645-658 `changelog` target runs `git cliff --unreleased --tag $(VERSION) --prepend CHANGELOG.md`, pinned to GIT_CLIFF_VERSION 2.13.1.
CHANGELOG.md:11 `## [Unreleased]` is empty.
findings.finding: The plan writes the 0.17.0 CHANGELOG section by hand from `git log v0.16.0..HEAD`. It skips the runbook's generate-then-curate step (`make changelog VERSION=v0.17.0`, git-cliff 2.13.1, which prepends a section built from the commits since the last tag). The runbook allows skipping that step only when `[Unreleased]` already holds curated entries, and here it is empty. With 138 commits, a fully hand-written section is the approach the runbook rejected as unsustainable. It is also more likely to miss entries than curating a section git-cliff has already grouped by commit type. The plan claims to follow docs/releasing.md but gives no reason for this deviation.
findings.location: Approach step 1 (CHANGELOG.md authoring); Context ('entries are curated from git log v0.16.0..HEAD')
scenarios: A user-visible fix or feature among the 138 commits is left out of the hand-written Added/Changed/Removed/Fixed lists, and the omission is permanent once published.
A future release uses git-cliff and its grouping and wording drift from this hand-written section.
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach step 1, replace 'write `## [0.17.0] - <release date>` ... with hand-curated entries' with: 'run `make changelog VERSION=v0.17.0` (git-cliff 2.13.1) to prepend the section, then hand-curate it into Added/Changed/Removed/Fixed, reconcile it against `git log v0.16.0..HEAD`, make sure a single empty `## [Unreleased]` sits above it, and add the `[0.17.0]: https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/compare/v0.16.0...v0.17.0` footer.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the bare autobump dispatch with the runbook's recovery sequence: check `.state`, enable the workflow if `disabled_inactivity` (escalate to the operator if `disabled_manually`), dispatch with `--ref main`, confirm the autobump run succeeded, and use the manual formula edit as the last resort.
evidence: Plan: "trigger `gh workflow run autobump.yml --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar` if the tap has not bumped"

docs/releasing.md §3 Recovery: `gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/actions/workflows/autobump.yml --jq .state` → `gh workflow enable ...` if disabled_inactivity → `gh workflow run ... --ref main` → `gh run list ... -L1   # expect success`
docs/releasing.md §3: "If a person disabled it (`disabled_manually`), the job fails instead of overriding that." and the 0.13.1-stuck incident (bug hedonistic-historical-graywolf).
findings.finding: The plan's Homebrew fallback is only `gh workflow run autobump.yml --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar` 'if the tap has not bumped'. The runbook explains that the release's `homebrew_tap` job fails, rather than overriding, when autobump.yml is `disabled_manually`. The tap's schedule also gets disabled after 60 days of inactivity. In either case the plan's single dispatch command fails or does nothing. It does not check `.state` first, re-enable a `disabled_inactivity` workflow, or confirm the autobump run succeeded.
scenarios: The `homebrew_tap` job failed because autobump.yml is disabled, so the plan's manual dispatch is rejected and the formula stays at 0.16.0.
findings.suggested_fix: In step 5, follow docs/releasing.md §3 'Recovery' if the tap has not bumped: `gh api repos/navapbc/homebrew-rebar/actions/workflows/autobump.yml --jq .state`; if `disabled_inactivity`, run `gh workflow enable autobump.yml --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar`; if `disabled_manually`, stop and ask the operator; then `gh workflow run autobump.yml --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar --ref main` and confirm `gh run list --repo navapbc/homebrew-rebar --workflow autobump.yml -L1` succeeded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Before dispatching, confirm `gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/commits/main --jq .sha` equals the recorded merge SHA (if main has moved on, decide and record whether the later commits ship in 0.17.0), and after dispatch check that the run's `headSha` equals that SHA.
evidence: Plan step 3: "`gh workflow run release.yml --ref main -f version=0.17.0`" with no precondition on the main HEAD.
Plan AC: "change number and merge SHA recorded in a comment" — but nothing ties the release run to that SHA.
docs/releasing.md: the `authorize` job checks the ref, version-lockstep, ancestry and env-preflight; none of them requires HEAD to equal the release commit.
findings.finding: Step 3 dispatches `release.yml --ref main` without checking that the GitHub mirror's `main` HEAD is the recorded merge SHA. The run builds whatever `main` points to at dispatch time. If the mirror has not synced yet, the run fails the version-lockstep guard (safe, but a wasted run and approval cycle). If other changes landed after the release commit, those commits ship under 0.17.0 even though they are not covered by the curated CHANGELOG, and the version guard cannot tell. The plan also never checks that the run's `headSha` matches the merge SHA it records.
findings.location: Approach step 3 (dispatch); AC 1 and the release.yml-run AC
scenarios: Another Gerrit change is submitted between the release commit's merge and the dispatch, so 0.17.0 publishes code the CHANGELOG does not describe.
The mirror lags behind Gerrit, so the authorize job's lockstep check fails against the 0.16.0 `pyproject.toml` and the run has to be repeated.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a precondition to step 3: '`gh api repos/navapbc/rebar/commits/main --jq .sha` equals the merge SHA recorded for the Gerrit change (if not, wait for the mirror, or reconcile the CHANGELOG with the extra commits); after dispatch, `gh run view $RUN --json headSha` matches it.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Change the MCP Registry check to the current `/v0.1/servers` endpoint (e.g. `/v0.1/servers/io.github.navapbc%2Frebar/versions/latest` or `/v0.1/servers?search=io.github.navapbc/rebar&version=latest`) and confirm it returns 0.17.0

docs/releasing.md:496 uses the same /v0 URL, so the plan copied the stale path from the docs.
Official registry aggregator docs list GET /v0.1/servers as the list endpoint; a 2026 guide says v0.1 is the live, current endpoint; deepwiki notes /v0/servers is 'also available at /v0.1/servers'.
findings.finding: The MCP Registry acceptance check queries the older `/v0/servers` path. Current registry documentation gives `/v0.1/servers` as the live API and the one aggregators should use. One registry-compatible implementation calls v0 the 'legacy, deprecated v0 MCP Registry API' and does not serve it. A secondary source says /v0 is still an alias for now. So whether the AC's check keeps working depends on a deprecated path, and nobody has confirmed it.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — MCP Registry line (also docs/releasing.md:496)
scenarios: The registry stops serving the deprecated /v0 alias, so the AC curl returns 404 or empty and a successful publish looks like a failure (or the operator gives up checking).
/v0 without version=latest returns several entries for the server, and the operator misreads which version is current.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `curl -s "https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/io.github.navapbc%2Frebar/versions/latest"` and check that `.server.version == "0.17.0"`; optionally update docs/releasing.md:496 to match.

findings.finding: Step 4 describes the pending-deployment approval request as a JSON body with only `environment_ids`. The repo's own procedure (docs/releasing.md:398) sends `{"environment_ids": [...], "state": "approved", "comment": "release X.Y.Z"}`. Someone who builds the request from the plan's summary would leave out the approval state, which the procedure relies on to actually approve the deployment.
scenarios: An automated session copies the plan's body description and posts only environment_ids. Based on the docs' note that malformed bodies get a 422, it would likely be rejected, leaving the run stuck at the pypi gate.
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite step 4 as: 'POST .../pending_deployments with `--input` JSON `{"environment_ids": [$ENV_ID], "state": "approved", "comment": "release 0.17.0"}` (ENV_ID read from GET pending_deployments `.[0].environment.id`), per docs/releasing.md.'
